#### Mixed Use Projects to be launched in FY26

Max One (Sector 16B, Noida)

Development Potential ~2.5 mn. sq. ft. ~1.2 mn sqft (unsold)

Gross Development Value

New Sales – Rs. 1,500 Cr+ Receivables – Rs. 500 Cr Rentals – Rs. 120 Cr+ Status RERA applied for Spanning ~2.5 mn sq. ft. across a ~10-acre land parcel, Max One will bring to life our vision of an integrated campus. A downtown experience that will host ultra-luxury residences, premium office spaces, curated high street retail and exclusive club facilities, thoughtfully blending our philosophy of LiveWell, WorkWell, and PlayWell. Situated at the edge of South Delhi and directly connected via the Delhi-Noida-Direct (DND) Flyway, the development is just steps from key metro stations, benefitting from unparalleled connectivity across Delhi NCR.

New Acquisition (Sector 105, Noida)

Development Potential ~2.6 mn. sq. ft. Mixed use Gross Development Value Sales – Rs. 3,000 Cr+ Rentals – Rs. 140 Cr+ Status RERA applied for Located in Sector 105, Noida, our upcoming mixed-use development spans ~10 acres with a development potential of 2.6 mn sq. ft., comprising 60% commercial and 40% residential space. With three open sides and a striking 75-meter frontage along the Noida-Greater Noida Expressway, the site enjoys excellent visibility and connectivity. Situated within a thriving residential and commercial micro-market, the offering will reflect our LiveWell and WorkWell philosophies, seamlessly integrating fitness, sports, and an active lifestyle into a thoughtfully curated urban experience.

#### Residential Projects to be launched in FY27

Estate 361 (Gurugram)

Development Potential ~4.0 mn. sq. ft.

Gross Development Value Rs. 9,000 Cr +

Status Phase 1 already launched

Expanding our footprint in Gurugram, Estate 361 is a LiveWell development located in Sector 36A along the Dwarka Expressway. Spread across ~18-acres with a development potential of ~4 mn sq. ft., Estate 361 is being thoughtfully envisioned around our LiveWell philosophy with the vision of bringing real wellbeing to real estate. Central to the design is a lush, 2-acre forest that will anchor the offering and foster holistic wellness for its community. We have already launched Phase I of the project in Q3FY26

#### LETTER TO THE SHAREHOLDERS

Dear Shareholders,

It is both an honour and a privilege to present our inaugural Integrated Annual Report as we mark a milestone year of purposeful growth and meaningful expansion. The theme, “Redefining Spaces, Pioneering Wellbeing”, captures the essence of our journey as we step into a new phase shaped by scale, clarity, sustainability, and execution.

FY2025 marks the beginning of Max Estates’ 3.0 execution phase. This was a strategic shift from being a single-project developer to becoming a purpose-driven real estate organisation delivering multiple large-scale projects across Delhi NCR.

This evolution has been grounded in capital discipline, capability enhancement, and an unwavering belief in our vision of bringing real wellbeing into real estate.

Global and Domestic Context: Resilience Amid Uncertainty

The global economic environment in 2024 remained complex and uneven. Several large economies faced long-term challenges. The United States stayed resilient, backed by consumer demand. Europe struggled to regain momentum and China’s real estate sector remained under pressure.

India, in contrast, outperformed global trends. Our economy remained stable with a positive outlook. GDP grew at an estimated 6.5%, making India one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world. Inflation eased, private and public investments picked up pace, and structural reforms continued to advance. Together, these factors strengthened India’s standing as a resilient, reliable growth engine in a challenging global context.

India’s real estate sector reflected this momentum. Institutional investments rose to $8.9 billion, a 51% increase over the previous year. Despite constrained supply, residential sales remained strong. The sector continues to be a key pillar to India’s economic and employment ecosystem.

The residential market saw a clear shift towards premium and luxury homes, driven by rising aspirations, greater affordability, and growing trust in branded developers. Commercial real estate also saw record momentum. India reached its highest-ever gross leasing volume of 79 million square feet, reflecting strong occupier confidence and the country’s rising appeal as a destination for Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

Scaling with Purpose: The Max Estates 3.0 Journey

As the market continues to evolve, we continue to grow with intention. The Max Estates 3.0 journey is grounded in strong fundamentals, including a focus on strategic locations and wellbeing-enabled ecosystems, high-quality design, customer-first experiences, and disciplined use of capital. This approach strengthens our foundation as a forward thinking real estate brand, ready to lead with purpose and clarity.

In line with our approach, FY2025 was a defining year for Max Estates—a year of moving from preparation to execution, from planning to performance, marking milestones across these key pillars.

» Our total portfolio grew from 8 million to over 17.1 million square feet, with a balanced mix of residential, commercial, and mixed-use developments across Noida, Gurugram, and Delhi. We evolved from managing one project to overseeing four operational assets, four under construction, and three in design. We acquired prime land and development rights across Delhi NCR, enhancing our vision to redefine real estate with contemporary design and a hospitality-led experience. This growth was shaped by deliberate strategic choices, rooted in product quality, innovation, and holistic customer experience.

India, in contrast, outperformed global trends. Our economy remained stable with a positive outlook. GDP grew at an estimated 6.5%, making India one of the fastest growing major economies in the world.

Mr. Analjit Singh Founder & Chairman, Max Group

Mr. Sahil Vachani Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Max Estates

We witnessed strong momentum in the residential segment. Pre-sales crossed ₹5,300 crore, a threefold rise from the previous year. Among our residential (LiveWell) offerings, Estate 128 in Noida is now fully sold, with Phase II launched at over 40% premium to Phase I, reaffirming the value of thoughtful design and customer-first experiences in residential communities. Estate 360 in Gurugram, Delhi NCR’s first intergenerational living concept, also saw a strong response. With 96% of its inventory sold, it recorded ₹4,634 crore in sales. Together, collections crossed ₹980 crore. It was a clear reflection of our execution and customer-centric approach.

In the commercial segment, we focused on creating spaces that deliver high-quality, differentiated experiences. Max Square in Noida reached over 99% leasing, at a 30% rental premium to its micro market. Max House Phase II in Delhi reached full occupancy within 12 months, at a 60% premium. Our commercial portfolio now spans over 6 million square feet across delivered, ongoing, and upcoming developments. Together, they carry a peak annuity rental potential of ₹720 crore. Each of our commercial assets is fully leased and home to a diverse mix of tenants. No single occupier holds more than 25% of space in any development, reaffirming that our leasing model remains resilient and built to last.

Capital Strength and Strategic Partnerships

FY2025 was also a year of strengthening our capital base. We raised over ₹1,300 crore of fresh capital through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), strategic investor participations, and sponsor capital commitments. The QIP alone accounted for ₹800 crore, with strong participation from marquee institutional investors. It signalled trust in our business model, our ability to deliver, and the long term direction we are building towards.

Our partnership with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL) also grew deeper. With a cumulative investment commitment of ₹1,800 crore, NYL now holds a 49% stake across our entire commercial portfolio, including upcoming mixed-use developments in Noida. Their partnership goes beyond capital. It is built on shared values, highest level of governance, aligned intent, and a belief in long-term value creation.

Together, these capital initiatives have fortified our balance sheet. As of March 31, 2025, we were net debt positive, with a cash surplus of ₹435 crore. This gives us the headroom to pursue new opportunities, manage risks with care, and continue scaling in a thoughtful, sustainable way.

Strengthening the Foundation for Execution at Scale

Our ability to deliver at scale is rooted in the strength of our people, structured processes, robust technology, and sound governance. This year, we onboarded over 120 professionals across functions, with focused hiring for the residential vertical. We also took steady steps toward building more inclusive teams, improving gender diversity across functions, and setting a clear target of 30% women’s representation over the next 24 months.

We partnered with In Tandem Global Consulting to co-author, “Concrete Change—A Study of the Economic Impact of Better Pay Parity & Inclusion of Women in Real Estate”. This is not just a milestone for the industry, but a reaffirmation of our belief that progress in business must go hand in hand with social progress.

To support consistent quality across projects, we institutionalised SOPs across 13 verticals of the real estate value chain. These were rigorously tested through internal audits to ensure operational rigour. Our digital roadmap continues to guide us across core functions, enabling greater project visibility, real-time decision-making, sharper operational efficiency, and enhanced stakeholder experience. We now use a suite of tools such as SAP, BIM, Salesforce, Zoho, and Autodesk to further strengthen our execution across the value chain.

On the sustainability front, we are working across the portfolio to conserve energy and water, reduce emissions, and minimise waste. We have already set reduction targets for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while actively baselining Scope 3 net zero targets.

On governance, we have continued to strengthen our Board with individuals who bring deep, cross sectoral expertise and strategic insight. Integrated Management Systems (IMS)

We embed sustainability into how we work every day through globally recognised IMS standards: ISO 9001 (Quality), ISO 14001 (Environmental), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety). These frameworks guide us to act responsibly, with both outcomes and processes shaped by care.

ISO 14001 helps us stay mindful of our environmental footprint by encouraging energy efficiency, reduced waste, conservation of natural resources, and thoughtful sourcing. We track our carbon footprint, keeping ourselves accountable to both our goals and our stakeholders.

ISO 45001 reflects our commitment to health, safety, and the wellbeing of our employees. A proactive risk management framework and ethical labour practices foster a culture where safety comes first, trust is built, and community relations are strengthened.

ISO 9001 ensures trust and safety through data integrity, strong internal controls, and continuous improvement. Standardised processes and clear responsibilities drive transparent governance, supporting alignment with global ESG reporting standards, such as the GRI, and enabling the tracking of measurable KPIs.

Strategic Benefits of IMS Implementation:

Strengthened Brand Reputation: Certifications reaffirm our commitment to high ESG standards, building stakeholder trust.

Investor Confidence: Robust, third-party validated systems bring transparency, aligning us with sustainable investment mandates.

Operational Efficiency: With one framework, we can anticipate risks, manage costs prudently, and deliver consistent quality.

Regulatory Compliance: IMS streamlines alignment to national and international regulations, helping us stay resilient in an evolving landscape.

Risk and Compliance

We uphold a strong commitment to environmental compliance and risk mitigation, particularly in alignment with evolving regulatory frameworks. During FY2025, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) enforced the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana during the winter months to address rising pollution levels. In adherence to these directives, Max Estates temporarily halted construction activities at select sites to prevent environmental degradation. While this led to short-term delays in construction timelines, it reflected our commitment to sustainable and responsible development.

Our sites were also reviewed under the Environment (Protection) Act. Every observation was met with care and swift action, and we remained fully compliant with the applicable legal and environmental standards.

Max Estates operates in a dynamic real estate environment influenced by various macroeconomic, demographic, and technological factors. With a deep understanding of these trends and the business needs they create, we have positioned ourselves to respond to evolving trends and fresh opportunities, particularly in the Delhi NCR region, through a dynamic approach in strategy

Despite global uncertainties, India’s macroeconomic landscape showed resilience in 2024, staying on track as one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated a Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 6.5%1. Strong domestic demand, ongoing infrastructure development, and easing inflation supported this momentum.

As global uncertainties continue, trade tensions and supply chain issues, and the announcement of new global tariffs by the United States may impact the external sector. The US has introduced a 10%2 universal tariff on imports. While India has a temporary exemption from the additional 26%3, we still face the baseline 10% duty on exports.

At home, the Union Budget’s tax incentives could boost GDP by 0.6-0.7%. Lower inflation, stable oil prices, and reduced borrowing rates are expected to enhance both spending and investment.

Looking ahead to FY2026, India’s outlook remains steady. Structural reforms, a growing workforce, and increased global interest in manufacturing continue to support momentum. Inflation is projected to ease to 4.0%4, while GDP growth is expected to remain steady at 6.5%5, as per the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)6.

The Indian real estate sector is poised for significant growth. It is projected to reach $1 trillion7 by 2030 and $7–10 trillion by 2047. Growth is driven by expanding infrastructure, rapid urbanisation, a young population, a growing manufacturing base, new jobs, and a sharper focus on sustainability and technology. The sector’s contribution to GDP is expected to stay steady at 6–8%. Government policies, such as the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) and the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), add to the momentum. The residential market is seeing healthy demand across all segments, while strong leasing demand supports commercial real estate, led by Global Capability Centres (GCCs) that span multiple sectors,

Max Estates is guided by the belief that people thrive when they LiveWell and WorkWell. With this philosophy at the core, we are well-positioned for sustainable growth in Delhi NCR. We benefit from a strong economic environment, a committed team of over 200 full-time professionals, technology-led operations, and a diversified portfolio across residential, commercial, and mixed-use segments.

Pre-sales performance has been strong. With Estate 128 completely sold out and Estate 360 nearing full capacity at 96%, we are gearing up for our next chapter of growth. To support this, we secured ₹800 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement, along with an additional ₹150 crore from preferential allotments to promoters and strategic investors.

Our long-term partnership with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL) Insurance includes a total investment commitment of ₹1,800 crore, with ₹550 crore earmarked for upcoming projects in Delhi One and Sector 105, Noida. As of March 31, 2025, Max Estates is net debt-positive with a healthy cash surplus of ₹435 crore. This provides the headroom to explore fresh opportunities and grow with discipline. Favourable urbanisation trends, changing consumer preferences and and strong policy support further reinforce our outlook. Max Estates is well-equipped to navigate macroeconomic uncertainties and continue its momentum through FY2026 and beyond.

Rapid Growth and Rising Demand for Premium Housing

India’s real estate sector is one of the country’s largest employment generators, with over 70 million people employed. Its contribution to GDP is expected to rise to around 13%8 by 2025, with the market size projected to hit $1 trillion by 2030. Institutional investments reached $8.9 billion in 2024, up 51%9 from 2023, driven by strong capital inflows. Rapid urbanisation is driving demand for housing and infrastructure, supported by both demand and supply enabling policies. The sector is also evolving with green building practices for the built environment to enable and not deteriorate better quality of life.

Outlook

Max Estates has built a diverse portfolio of over 17 million square feet across Delhi NCR, covering commercial, residential, and mixed-use assets. After delivering a series of premium projects in the region, we are now focused on accelerating growth through carefully selected mixed-use ventures. The plan is to add at least 3 million square feet annually, and further strengthen our foothold in key micro-markets of Delhi NCR.

Office Space Demand and Occupier-led Growth

India’s office market hit a record 79 million square feet of absorption in 2024, marking a 17%12 year on-year increase. This growth was led by domestic companies, global entrants, and Global Capability Centres, which leased 29 million square feet and are expected to continue holding a 35 to 40% share. The appeal lies in India’s deep talent pool, tech ecosystem, and competitive rentals. Across the board, demand is shifting towards green-certified, tech-enabled spaces that reflect a growing emphasis on quality and sustainability in the post-pandemic world.

Outlook

Max Estates has curated its commercial portfolio to deliver premium workspace experiences. Max Square was delivered in just 30 months and currently is 99% leased, at a 30% premium. Its tenants include Adobe, NDTV, Cloudangles, and AML Rightsource. Max House Phase II, delivered in Q3 FY2024, achieved full occupancy within 12 months at a 60% premium. Max Towers and Max House Phase I remain fully leased at 25–30% above market rates. No tenant holds more than 25% of any single asset. Tenant retention remains high, with turnover close to zero. This reflects the strength, quality, and long-term relevance of the portfolio.

Urban Demand Surge

India’s residential real estate market saw strong growth in 2024, with housing sales reaching 4.59 lakh units, 76%10 higher than 2019 levels. Luxury and super-luxury homes made up 30% of the new supply, rising from just 11% in 2019, while affordable housing dropped to 16%11. This shift reflects rising incomes, stronger homebuyer confidence, and growing demand from affluent buyers, NRIs, and HNIs. The trend is likely to continue through FY2026, supported by better infrastructure and a growing preference for larger homes.

Outlook

Max Estates recorded a landmark year in the residential segment in FY2025. Bookings crossed ₹5,300 crore, three times higher than FY2024. This underscored the strength of our product-market fit. Estate 128 in Noida is fully sold, while Phase II achieved a price premium of over 40% compared to Phase I. In Gurugram, Estate 360, Delhi NCR’s first intergenerational residential development of its kind, was 96% sold by March 2025. Together, these projects contributed ₹980 crore in collections. The results reflect Max Estates’ distinct, high-quality approach to residential development.

Sustainability and ESG Compliance

Awareness around the environmental impact of the built environment is steadily rising. This has led to increased regulatory scrutiny and growing investor focus on sustainable construction. India now has more than 60013 IGBC-rated green buildings, most of which deliver energy savings of 40–50% and water savings of 30–35%. These numbers reflect both widespread adoption and sector-wide readiness. GRESB standards are also gaining importance, with higher ratings seen as a mark of responsible leadership.

Outlook

Rooted in Max Group’s core values of Sevabhav (Service), Excellence, and Credibility, and shaped by its LiveWell and WorkWell philosophy, Max Estates weaves sustainability into every development. The central forest courtyard at Max Square, spanning 11,000 square feet, and the in-house engagement platform Pulse, which hosted over 200 wellbeing events and engaged 8,400 employees with an Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 6.9 in FY2025, a very high scale by global standards. This shows our on-ground commitment. Since 2021, we have held a GRESB 4-star rating, alongside certifications from LEED, IGBC, ISO, and WELL. We now aim for a GRESB14

5-star rating in 2025. Max Estates is also formalising its Net Zero targets for Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2040 in alignment with SBTi. Scope 3 emissions are now being tracked, and Life Cycle Assessments are underway across the portfolio. Behind these efforts is a combination of strong systems, growing in-house expertise, and a passionate team. We are all working towards the shared goal of improving lives through thoughtfully designed spaces.

Digital Transformation and Property Technology

Digitalisation is reshaping every stage of the real estate journey, from how properties are discovered and built to how they are sold and serviced after handover. Real estate firms are increasingly turning to PropTech and digital tools to improve everything from listings to construction monitoring.

Outlook

Max Estates has adopted digital innovation across the business. We use platforms such as SAP, BIM, Salesforce, Zoho, Autodesk, FacTech, Smart Joules, SAP Ariba, and Reloy to streamline workflows, improve collaboration, and support faster, more informed decision-making. These tools are helping us drive efficiency, reduce costs, grow revenues, and offer an enhanced customer experience. A structured three-year digital roadmap is now in place to further support scale readiness. At the same time, Max Estates is deploying technology-led solutions to optimise energy use, water management, and waste handling. These efforts reinforce our commitment to sustainable operations.

Policy and Regulatory Reforms

The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act15 has played a key role in building buyer confidence. Surveys and academic studies show its positive impact in speeding up dispute resolution and reducing unsold inventory by bringing greater transparency into the system and disciplined capital deployment. For example, in Maharashtra, RERA now issues user-friendly registration certificates that clearly outline project details and require developers to share regular progress updates with homebuyers.

Outlook

Max Estates takes great pride in meeting the highest standards set by RERA and all other applicable laws including building bye-laws, environment-related compliances and labour-related best practices. This compliance reflects our commitment to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and professional excellence. By ensuring clear, timely communication throughout every stage of the property journey, Max Estates creates an environment where customers feel valued and confident in their decisions.

Max Estates continues to stand out by creating integrated spaces that are thoughtfully designed and future-ready. We aim to become Delhi NCR’s leading real estate brand.

In FY2026, Max Estates will focus on scaling pre-sales to ₹6,000–6,500 crore, securing 2,00,000 square feet of pre-leased space and adding 3 million square feet of new opportunities. Our key priorities include financial closures, securing a GRESB 5-star rating, expanding digital systems, enhancing risk management and talent development, and expanding our brand footprint beyond Delhi NCR.

Max Estates’ materiality assessment involved an internal desk review benchmarking best practices from industry peers, covering environmental, social, and governance pillars. Moving forward, we intend to integrate these material topics into our strategic planning, establish science-based targets, and implement robust governance structures to ensure accountability. We will monitor progress through regular data collection and audits, leveraging sustainability committees for ongoing oversight and continuous improvement. This approach, grounded in peer-led best practices, will enhance transparency, stakeholder engagement, and long-term value creation.

Modular Construction Pilot

We are driving construction excellence through a modular and off-site strategy that delivers speed, precision, and sustainability. We prefabricate temporary structures and formwork off-site, which minimises material waste and reduces on-site disruption. Our fully unitised façades are manufactured and assembled with a high level of quality control, while aluminium modular formwork shortens slab cycle times significantly.

We plan every step in advance and maintain a two month material buffer to stay ahead of potential delays. On-site batching plants ensure a steady concrete supply, and our equipment is regularly calibrated for consistency. Modular techniques give us greater design flexibility, support ergonomic handling, and enhance worker safety.

Before adopting any new material, we conduct thorough case studies and due diligence. This disciplined approach reflects our commitment to quality, efficiency, and innovation in every build.

Guided by IGBC/LEED guidelines, we prioritise green-certified, low-VOC products and prefer local suppliers to minimise logistics emissions and support local economies. We embrace a circular-resource mindset by prioritising the principles of reduce, reuse, and recycle. Reusing materials on-site, such as dismantled exhibition structures, is common practice. Our Circular Economy Policy highlights the importance of cutting waste and repurposing materials, helping us embed sustainability in our everyday business.

Every Max Estates development reflects the philosophy that built spaces should harmonise and not burden natural ecosystems. Our water-sensitive urban design keeps operations efficient while protecting and conserving water, supporting our long-term water security in its regions where we operate.

Water Consumption Policy and Strategic Oversight

We have introduced a suite of water-efficient technologies and sustainable design strategies across our developments, aiming to lower our water footprint while meeting the daily needs of tenants and users. Our measures focus on improving demand-side efficiency and strengthening supply-side augmentation.

Sustainable Water Infrastructure

Key interventions include:

Max Estates reports 100% water recycling across the entire portfolio. All facilities have achieved zero liquid discharge, with treated wastewater being fully reused for flushing and landscaping. Out of 112,450 litres of water used in FY2025, around 15% (16,830 litres) came from STP recycled water. Rainwater harvesting, efficient waste management and 100% waste diversion from landfills are standard. We aim to earn a 5-star GRESB rating, building on our 4-star achievement in 2023 while we ensure a Green Building certification for all our assets.

Low-flow Water Fixtures: Use of low-flow faucets, waterless urinals, and pressure-regulated fixtures in all washrooms to cut water consumption at the source.

Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD): All our projects follow a ZLD model, ensuring no untreated wastewater is released. Sewage is treated and reused within premises, dramatically lowering freshwater withdrawal.

Greywater Recycling: Treated greywater is used for flushing and landscaping, easing demand on potable water usage.

Rainwater Harvesting: Installed across multiple developments, rainwater is collected and stored for reuse in irrigation and other non-potable uses.

Smart Metering: Floor-wise meters lets us track water usage in real-time which helps us detect anomalies, and optimise every drop.

Sustainable Procurement

Our Procurement Policy emphasises sourcing goods and services that are environmentally friendly, locally sourced, and low-carbon. This sustainable approach prioritises the well-being of communities and aligns with our vision of achieving sustainable development through low-impact initiatives. Extraction, production, and transport of raw materials used in construction require significant energy, often from fossil fuels. By reusing and recycling materials, we reduce the demand for virgin resources, lower embodied carbon, and cut the energy needed for material production, contributing to a smaller carbon footprint. Recycling steel, aluminium, and concrete saves far more energy than producing them from raw resources.

We choose materials with care, following international guidelines on green building standards and favouring local sourcing of products and materials. With this small step, we support the local economy and make a small but relevant impact in reducing our transportation footprint. Our execution process also backs the broader ESG and community development goals, such as local employment, resource efficiency, and environmentally responsible practices.

#### RISK MANAGEMENT

At Max Estates, we see risk management as an integral part of how we work and make decisions. As we grow across the Delhi-NCR region, we navigate a wide and evolving range of risks, from regulatory changes and environmental factors to economic shifts and challenges to our reputation. To stay ahead, we keep our approach dynamic, updating our strategies to match changing realities while staying true to our strategic goals, operational resilience, and the trust of our stakeholders.

Strong risk management not only safeguards value. It also creates space for sustainable growth. Our approach lays equal emphasis on spotting potential risks early and responding with agility. This helps us remain prepared for disruptions while continuing to create thoughtful spaces that stand the test of time.

Risk Management Framework

Our risk management framework is designed for strong cross-functional coordination. This ensures that potential risks are identified, escalated, and mitigated effectively in every part of our operations. The framework covers a wide range of areas, including operational hazards, supply chain bottlenecks, regulatory compliance, and matters affecting our reputation.

Risk Governance Process

Layers of Risk Governance Risk Register Update – Quarterly Every quarter, the risk register SPOC undertakes a cycle of updates to the risk register in collaboration with the respective functional owners of the risk buckets.

Functional Risk Review – Monthly During the functional reviews held every month with the CEO and COO, all functions review the key risks and the respective mitigation strategies.

Cross Functional Risk Review – Weekly As part of the weekly cross-functional forum held every Monday morning, the key risks are brought in turn for a cross-functional review of the mitigation plan.

Risk Committee Review – Biannually Every six months, the red flags for the Company are reviewed as part of the risk committee meeting to seek the committee’s guidance on the way forward.

162 163

Identification

We actively identify risks through ongoing analysis and real-time monitoring, ensuring we catch issues early and act promptly.

Mitigation

We act quickly to contain risks while building stronger systems for the future. Mitigation is part of how we work every day.

Escalation

We have a clear, multi-layered escalation framework to keep risk management proactive and responsive.

Risk Register Each department maintains an updated Risk Register through regular SWOT analyses. Each risk is assessed for how soon it might occur, how likely it is, and its impact and severity.

Real-time Monitoring An external partner manages a dedicated Online Reputation Management (ORM) tracker that monitors digital platforms round the clock. It swiftly flags potential reputation concerns, such as negative press, viral complaints, or social media backlash, enabling prompt action.

This approach supports Max Estates in protecting operations, safeguarding stakeholders, and continuing as a responsible leader in India’s real estate sector.

Digitalisation Upgrading digital tools to automate compliance workflows, monitoring related party transactions (RPT), and controlling insider trading.

Independent Oversight Independent audits for related-party transactions will ensure greater transparency.

Broadened Risk Culture We aim to build a stronger risk-aware mindset across business planning, day-to-day operations, and stakeholder communications.

Short-term Response When negative press or a social backlash hits, we run our rapid response playbook, with social media containment, clear official press lines, and customer grievance redressal mechanisms.

Long-term Measures We use trends from the Risk Register to guide longer-term strategies, such as reshaping policy, enhancing stakeholder engagement, and strengthening our business continuity plans.

Operational Hazards and Vendor Risks We review operational hazards, supply chain dependencies and vendor risks continuously. Mitigation is embedded in project delivery, vendor selection and contract clauses so risk is managed at source.

Strengthening Governance

We are sharpening our risk governance with clear, focused steps:

Structured Protocols High-severity risks, especially those that can affect reputation, are escalated immediately to cross functional teams through well-established procedures.

Monthly Risk Reviews In monthly functional reviews with the CEO and COO, each function reviews its key risks and the mitigation strategies in place.

Quarterly Risk Reviews Every quarter, our leadership reviews the Company’s risk register, ensuring ongoing oversight and reprioritisation of risks with the changing business environment.

Weekly Risk Reviews In the weekly cross-functional forum held every Monday morning, teams bring forward their key risks in turn for review and discussion on mitigation plans.

Biannual Risk Committee Review Every six months, the Company’s red flags are presented to the risk committee to seek their guidance on the way forward.

Max Estates: Positioned to Lead the Next Phase of Real Estate Growth in NCR

Bringing Real Well-being to Real Estate

FY2025 marked a significant phase of growth for Max Estates, reaffirming the company’s strong conviction in the real estate opportunity within Delhi-NCR. Staying true to its core philosophies of WorkWell & LiveWell, the company continued its strategic trajectory—expanding its development portfolio from 8 million square feet in FY2024 to over 17 million square feet in FY2025 across residential, commercial, and mixed-use segments.

This year was particularly notable as the company entered the mixed-use development space through two marquee acquisitions, furthering its vision of delivering differentiated real estate experiences that integrate cutting-edge design with exceptional hospitality and a focus on wellbeing.

Strategic Acquisitions: Driving Portfolio Growth Max Estates made bold, forward-looking moves in FY2025, acquiring prime land parcels and development rights across Delhi-NCR with the following acquisitions:

Delhi One, Sector 16B, Noida – The Company successfully acquired the Delhi One project after receiving final approvals under the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code from Hon’ble NCLT and Hon’ble NCLAT in February 2023 and October 2024, respectively. The project is an integrated mixed-use development that will have ultra-luxury serviced residences, premium office spaces, and retail spaces. This strategic acquisition offers significant development potential of about 2.5 million square feet, inclusive of already sold units. The project is expected to generate a total sales potential of approximately ₹2,000 crore, along with an annuity rental income potential of around ₹120 crore.

Sector 105, Noida – Marking the first acquisition under government auction, the Company acquired a 10.33acre parcel along the Noida-Greater Noida Expressway for ₹711 crore through a competitive auction. It has a development potential of 2.6 million square feet with 40 per cent residential (group housing) and 60 per cent commercial (including office and retail). The project has a Gross Development Value (GDV) potential of over approximately ₹2,500 crore and an annuity rental income potential of more than ₹140 crore.

Estate 361, Sector 36A, Gurugram – Adjacent to its flagship residential project Estate 360 in Gurugram, the company acquired an 18-acre residential parcel with development potential of 4 mn square feet, expanding its footprint to nearly 30 acres in this emerging luxury corridor on the Dwarka Expressway. Estate 361 adds a GDV potential of ₹9,000 crore, bringing the combined Gurugram development potential to over ₹13,000 crore across 6.4 million square feet.

Together, these acquisitions expanded the company’s total portfolio to 17 million square feet, laying a strong foundation for its long-term growth strategy of adding at least 3 million square feet of development portfolio annually across residential and commercial asset classes.

FY2025 Marks a Milestone Year of Execution at Scale and Robust Pre-Sales In FY2025, the company delivered strong operational performance across its portfolio. Estate 128, Noida, achieved Phase II bookings of ₹894 crore, exceeding its target of ₹800 crore. Spanning 10 acres, the project has now evolved into a fully integrated premium residential community with a total booking value clocked of~ ₹2,734 crore and is 100 per cent sold. Estate 360 in Gurugram maintained strong momentum, recording ₹4,634 crore in pre-sales with 96 per cent of the inventory sold. Between Estate 128 and Estate 360, the company did ₹980 Cr of collections.

In the commercial segment, Max Square in Noida— designed around the theme “Where Nature Meets Work”—achieved over 99 per cent leasing across ~0.7 million square feet, with rentals commanding a 30 per cent premium over the micro-market. Similarly, Max House Phase II in Okhla was fully leased at rentals 60 per cent above the market average, underscoring the demand for well-designed, high-quality office spaces.

Backed by a strong team of a strand team of over 200 full time professionals, a robust zero net-debt balance sheet, and technology-led operations with sustainability embedded at the core, the company is well-positioned to execute and operate at scale with four operational assets and construction progressing steadily on four large developments with three more currently in the design phase. Max Estates is strengthening its focus on the LiveWell and WorkWell philosophy, embedding it across every aspect — from location and design to operations, materials, and beyond.

A Purpose-led Organisation with Strong Governance

India’s Growth Story: Strong Momentum and a Stable Outlook

Max Estates is committed to bringing the Max Group’s core values—Sevabhav (Service), Excellence, and Credibility—to the Indian real estate landscape. The Company is guided by a renewed purpose: “Enhancing quality of life through the spaces we create”. Over the past year, the Company has institutionalised robust systems, built organisational depth, and attracted high quality talent to enable execution at scale and deliver on its long-term vision.

The global economy in 2024 navigated a complex environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, uncertainties, rapid technological shifts, and changing consumer behaviours. The U.S. economy showed notable resilience with 2.8%1 Real GDP growth, supported by strong domestic demand and consumer spending. In contrast, Europe experienced a sluggish recovery, growing at just 0.8%2 , hindered by structural headwinds in energy-intensive sectors. Germany, the region’s largest economy, slipped into its second consecutive year of recession, while China’s recovery was constrained by persistent issues in its property sector. Amid these challenges, India and Southeast Asia emerged as key global growth drivers, benefiting from rising consumption, accelerated digital adoption, and sustained infrastructure investments.

In 2024, the Indian economy demonstrated strong resilience amid a challenging global environment. With GDP growth estimated at 6.5% by the IMF, India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies, supported by robust domestic consumption, steady services exports, and a rebound in investment activity, accelerated digital adoption, robust services, increased public and private infrastructure spending, and growing momentum in manufacturing.

Focused Strategy: One Region, Multiple Asset Classes

Max Estates has also partnered with the Latika Centre for Inclusion, reaffirming our commitment to building universally accessible environments that support and empower specially abled individuals. As part of this initiative, a dedicated 56,000 sq. ft. campus is being developed, featuring activity rooms, therapy and counselling units, a library, physiotherapy and sensory areas, a family resource centre, an inclusive playground, training halls, and a ramp-accessible building.

Max Estates continues to follow a focused strategy of: “One region, multiple asset classes”. We have curated a portfolio of 17 million square feet, which is well diversified in terms of geographical footprint across Delhi–NCR (Gurugram, Noida and Delhi), asset class (both residential, commercial and mixed use) and risk spectrum (delivered, under construction and design). In a region with limited presence of credible, consumer centric developers, Max Estates aims to fill the gap by delivering holistic, design-led, wellness and hospitality driven experiences. Anchored in the WorkWell and LiveWell philosophies, the company aspires to become a leading real estate brand in Delhi-NCR.

Looking ahead, the outlook for FY2026 remains optimistic, driven by continued structural reforms, a young and growing workforce, and rising global interest in India as a reliable alternative manufacturing base. Consumer price inflation in India is expected to gradually decline, easing from 5.4% in FY2024 to 4.9% in FY2025, and further moderating to 4.0% in FY2026. According to the Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), the Indian economy is likely to sustain its current growth trajectory, with GDP projected to grow at 6.5% year-on-year in FY2026, maintaining the momentum seen in previous years.

For India, these global developments bring both risks and opportunities. While the imposition of U.S. tariffs on various goods raises concerns for global trade, India’s economy remains relatively insulated due to its higher share of service exports, which are less affected by such barriers. S&P Global forecasts India’s GDP growth at 6.5% for FY2026, supported by cooling inflation and fiscal support announced in the Union Budget. Additionally, U.S.-China trade tensions are creating new avenues for India, particularly in electronics manufacturing. With electronics exports reaching $20.4 billion in FY2024 and the continued rollout of Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, India is well-positioned to expand its manufacturing base. While global GDP growth is projected to slow from 3.3%3 in 2024 to 2.8%3 in 2025, India’s diversified economy and proactive policy measures suggest continued resilience and momentum.

Overall, India’s growth trajectory remains strong, as its economic structure adapts to the shifting global landscape with a focus on domestic strength and future-oriented development.

Real Estate Emerges as Key Economic Engine with Rising Investments and Urbanisation

India’s real estate sector demonstrated strong momentum in 2024, reflecting growing investor confidence and sustained economic activity. The sector is one of the largest employment generators in the country, employing over 704 million people, and is expected to contribute around 13%4 to India’s GDP by 2025, with the market size projected to reach USD 1 trillion4 by 2030. Institutional investments surged to USD 8.95 billion in 2024, marking a 51% increase from 2023, highlighting robust capital inflows. Urbanisation remains a key demand driver, with over 50%6 of India’s population expected to live in urban areas by 2047, fuelling the need for housing, infrastructure, and services across major and emerging cities. Government initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) continue to promote affordable housing, while growing adoption of PropTech and sustainable, green building practices reflect the sector’s evolving focus on technology and environmental responsibility. Foreign direct investment remains strong, with 100%

FDI allowed under the automatic route for townships, housing, and built-up infrastructure, further boosting growth prospects.

Looking ahead, the outlook for FY2026 remains positive, supported by recent monetary easing from the Reserve Bank of India and ongoing infrastructure investments. While the sector faces challenges like rising input costs and regulatory complexities, a gradual moderation in price growth is expected to balance demand and supply. Additionally, the real estate industry is undergoing a transformation, emphasising innovation in design, sustainability, and digital integration to meet changing consumer preferences. Overall, real estate continues to be a vital pillar of India’s economic expansion, driven by structural demand, demographic shifts, and policy support that collectively position it for sustained growth in the years ahead.

Customer Experience

Empirical evidence suggests that there is a strong correlation between the built environment and the quality of life experienced by its users. Thus, enhancing customer experience through well-designed spaces can directly impact the overall health and well-being of end users.

At Max Estates, we’ve paid close attention to creating a unique confluence of spaces that enable collaboration, innovation, and community, that are not just functional and aesthetically pleasing, but also environmentally sustainable, and designed to promote the holistic well-being of our users. Guided by our philosophy of WorkWell and LiveWell, we create differentiated working and living experiences by moving beyond the conventional separation of work, life, and well being, and paying attention to the entire spectrum of well-being across physical, emotional, social, and environmental aspects. Our developments personify our wellbeing orientation and bring our WorkWell and LiveWell philosophies to life.

Our focus on WorkWell and LiveWell is anchored around 9 pillars - empathetic hospitality, elemental harmony, generosity, inclusivity, peace of mind, belonging, Intentional Design, sustainability and food & nutrition. For instance, we integrate nature meaningfully into our designs, exemplified by the ~11,000 square feet forest courtyard at Max Square.

Our in-house engagement vertical, Pulse, breathes life into our buildings by curating a collection of events and activities that nurture occupants to be healthier and happier. Pulse orchestrated 200+ Events, driving 8,400+ tenant employee engagements in FY2025 across all our operational assets. All of this has resulted in top-notch NPS9. score of 6.9/10

People

To support execution at scale, Max Estates has significantly strengthened its organisational capabilities over the past year, with a focused effort on attracting high-quality talent, particularly to build out the residential vertical. Over 120 experienced professionals have been onboarded in FY2025 across key functions, blending real estate and cross-industry expertise. We continue to invest in leadership development and capability building through structured learning programs, ensuring our teams are equipped to deliver on the scale and ambition of our growing portfolio.

Max Estates has made significant strides across its core strategic pillars, building a strong foundation for scalable execution and sustained value creation.

Growth

Max Estates has built a well-diversified and scalable real estate portfolio across Delhi NCR, spanning commercial, residential, and mixed-use developments. Following the successful execution of premium commercial projects in Delhi and Noida and the launch of differentiated residential communities in Noida and Gurugram, the company has strategically expanded into mixed-use assets through targeted acquisitions. With a current portfolio of ~17 million square feet, Max Estates is positioned to accelerate its growth momentum by adding at least 3 million square feet annually across both residential and commercial segments, thereby strengthening its presence across key micro-markets in the region.

Capital

To fuel its next phase of growth, Max Estates successfully raised ₹800 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), which garnered strong participation from leading domestic and global institutional investors such as Nippon, Invesco, ITI Mutual Fund, and Trust Mutual Fund—reflecting robust confidence in the Company’s business model, execution capability, and long-term potential.

In addition to the QIP, the Company raised further capital of ₹150 crore through preferential allotments to promoters and strategic investors. New York Life (NYL), a long-standing partner, deepened its commitment by acquiring a 49 per cent stake in two SPVs holding Max Towers and Max House (Phase I & II) for a total amount of ₹388 Cr.

Collectively, the equity infusion from the QIP, preferential allotment, and NYL’s investment brings in over ₹1,300 crore of fresh capital, significantly enhancing the Company’s financial flexibility to pursue new development opportunities and scale operations.

With existing stakes in Max Square, Max Square Two, and Max District, Gurugram development, NYL now holds a 49 per cent interest across the entire commercial real estate portfolio of Max Estates. Their cumulative investment commitment stands at ₹1,800 crore, including ₹550 crore towards upcoming mixed use projects at Delhi One and Sector 105, Noida.

In parallel, Max Estates continues to adopt capital efficient models, including Joint Development Agreements (JDAs), which are being successfully implemented in its ongoing residential projects in Gurugram.

Execution

Max Estates has transitioned from executing one project at a time to managing a robust multi-project portfolio. As of FY2025, we have 4 operational projects, 4 under construction projects and 3 under design projects. All under-construction projects remain broadly on track in terms of both timelines and budgets, reflecting disciplined project management and operational rigour.

Residential performance - Max Estates delivered strong execution outcomes in FY2025, with total bookings surpassing ₹5,000 crore, approximately 3x of last FY2024 — demonstrating the strength of our product market fit and customer trust. Estate 128, our first residential development in Noida, is fully sold. Phase II of Estate 128 saw a 40 %+ price premium over Phase I, reflecting strong demand for design and hospitality led end-user-focused residential developments. Estate 360 in Gurugram — NCR’s first intergenerational living concept- is 96 per cent sold as of March 2025. Between Estate 128 and Estate 360, the company did ₹980 Cr of collections. These results validate our approach of delivering differentiated, high-quality residential offerings.

On the commercial side, Max Square was completed in a record 30 months and is over 99 per cent leased as of June 2025 at a 30 per cent premium to the micro market, attracting marquee occupiers such as Adobe, NDTV, CloudAngles, and AML Rightsource. Max House Phase II was delivered in Q3FY2024 and fully leased within 12 months at a 60 per cent rental premium. Our legacy commercial assets, Max Towers and Max House Phase I, continue to operate at full occupancy with lease rentals 25–30 per cent above market, supported by a diversified tenant base of leading domestic and international firms. We have built a well diversified portfolio of office and retail clients, with no single tenant occupying more than 25% of respective buildings and near-zero attrition — a reflection of the enduring appeal of our spaces and the quality of our tenant engagements, enabling them to truly WorkWell.We are deeply committed to our key pillars of execution: people, process, sustainability, digital

Sustainability remains central to our operations. #### Corporate Governance Report

##### OUR CORPORATE GOVERNANCE PHILOSOPHY

Your Company maintains a steadfast commitment to upholding the highest standards of Corporate Governance. We believe that exemplary governance serves as a cornerstone for value-oriented leadership, fostering accountability, transparency, and ethical conduct throughout our organization.

We have been dedicated to implementing a comprehensive governance framework across the Group. This journey has involved the introduction of transformative initiatives focused on three pivotal aspects of governance:

» Capital Management Discipline: We prioritize prudent capital management practices to ensure the responsible allocation of resources and sustainable growth. » Performance Management Excellence: Through robust performance management systems, we continuously monitor and enhance the performance of our businesses to drive efficiency and competitiveness. » Stakeholder Value Creation: Our efforts are geared towards creating sustained value for all stakeholders, fostering long-term relationships built on trust and mutual benefit.

We remain committed in our pursuit of excellence in Corporate Governance, recognizing its pivotal role in driving our continued success and fostering stakeholder confidence.

BOARD ARCHITECTURE

Your Company has undertaken significant steps to optimize board structures, ensuring they embody the ideal composition for effective governance. This includes:

» Independent Directorship: We have strived to achieve the optimal balance by appointing a suitable number of Independent Directors, bringing diverse expertise and perspectives to the table. » Board Diversity: Recognizing the value of diverse viewpoints, we have worked to ensure representation across various functional and industry domains within our boards. » Active Lead Directors: Each board benefits from the presence of an engaged lead Director, facilitating proactive governance and strategic oversight.

» Separation of Roles: To reinforce accountability and decision-making clarity, we have separated the roles of CEOs and Chairmen within our boards. Moreover, we have clearly defined the board’s role in key areas such as: » Strategy Formulation: Boards actively contribute to shaping strategic direction and long-term goals. » Financial Monitoring: Rigorous oversight mechanisms are in place to monitor the financial health of our companies. » Leadership Development: Boards are actively involved in fostering a culture of leadership excellence and talent development. » Risk Management: Comprehensive risk management strategies are formulated and monitored by the board to safeguard our interests. » Succession Planning: Robust succession plans are developed and overseen by the board, ensuring continuity of leadership and organizational stability. Through these initiatives, we aim to bolster governance effectiveness, enhance stakeholder confidence, and drive sustainable value creation across our Group.

BOARD PROCESSES

Our commitment to optimizing the effectiveness of our Board extends to various facets, including:

» Director Onboarding: We ensure a smooth onboarding process for new Directors, equipping them with the necessary knowledge and resources to fulfill their roles effectively. » Board Education and Engagement: Continuous education and engagement initiatives are undertaken to enhance Directors’ understanding of our business and industry landscape, enabling informed decision making. » Promoting Independence: We foster an environment that encourages independent thinking and actions, adhering strictly to our code of conduct to uphold ethical standards and integrity. » Meeting Efficiency: Key operational aspects, such as crafting comprehensive meeting agendas and facilitating the flow of timely and relevant information to the Board, are meticulously managed to optimize the Board’s time and focus on critical business areas.

» External Expertise: External speakers are invited to share insights and best practices, enriching the Board’s discussions and keeping them informed of industry trends and benchmarks. » Comprehensive Board Materials: Board materials are curated to be comprehensive, concise, and strategically relevant, facilitating meaningful discussions and decision-making. » Sub-committee Review: Material matters are thoroughly reviewed by specific Board sub committees, comprising a balanced mix of Non executive and Independent Directors with relevant expertise. Detailed charters are in place for each sub committee, outlining their roles and responsibilities. Through these measures, we ensure that our Board functions optimally, with a focus on strategic oversight, value creation, and prudent governance across all critical aspects of our business.

BOARD EFFECTIVENESS

To continually enhance Board effectiveness, we employ several mechanisms: » Annual Evaluation: An annual evaluation of Board Members is conducted to assess performance and identify areas for improvement, ensuring ongoing alignment with organizational goals and values. » Inter-Company Board Movements: When necessary, inter-company Board movements are facilitated to ensure that each Board is composed of members who bring relevant expertise and are fully engaged in decision-making processes. » Performance Improvement Mechanisms: Various mechanisms are in place to improve Board performance, including: − Clear Standards of Conduct: We establish clear standards of conduct and behavior to guide Board members in fulfilling their responsibilities with integrity and professionalism. − Governance Interventions: A calendar of key governance interventions, such as strategy-setting sessions and risk management sessions, is set to ensure that the Board remains proactive in addressing critical issues and opportunities. − Consequence Management: Ef fective consequence management processes are implemented to address deviations from expected behavior or performance standards, fostering accountability and continuous improvement. By implementing these measures, we aim to continuously strengthen our Boards’ effectiveness, enabling them to make informed decisions that drive sustainable business growth and value creation.

BOARD OF DIRECTORS

The Board of Directors (“the Board”), set up by the shareholders as the top governing body, plays an important role in setting the Company’s vision and protecting the interests of all stakeholders. The Board guides the Company’s main goals, supports Management to carry out plans, and reviews progress against set targets. This shared oversight helps the Company stay strong, responsible, and focused on creating long-term value for shareholders, employees, customers, and the community.

Qualified Institutions Placement

During the year under review, the Company successfully completed a Qualified Institutions Placement (“QIP”) on September 3, 2024. Pursuant to the QIP, 1,33,89,121 equity shares of face value ₹10 each were allotted to 31 Qualified Institutional Buyers at an issue price of ₹597.50 per share (including a premium of ₹587.50 per share), representing a discount of ₹31.24 (approximately 4.97%) to the floor price of ₹628.74 per share, in compliance with Regulation 176(1) of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 (“SEBI ICDR”). The QIP raised an aggregate of ₹800 crore, with application monies received in the ‘Max Estates Limited – QIP Escrow Account’. In accordance with Regulation 173A of the SEBI ICDR and Regulation 32 of the Listing Regulations, the Company appointed CARE Ratings Limited as the Monitoring Agency for utilisation of the proceeds.

Convertible Warrants

Further, the Company, on October 29, 2024, allotted 22,83,104 convertible warrants (“Warrants”) at an issue price of ₹657 per Warrant, aggregating to approximately ₹150 crore, in compliance with Regulation 169(2) of the SEBI ICDR, the Act, and other applicable laws. Each Warrant entitles the holder to apply for and be allotted one fully paid-up equity share of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹647, at any time within 18 months from the date of allotment. In accordance with Regulation 169(5) of the SEBI ICDR, the Company appointed CARE Ratings Limited as the Monitoring Agency to oversee utilisation of the ₹37.50 crore upfront amount (representing 25% of the Warrant issue price) received in the designated account.

Pursuant to Regulation 32(4) of the Listing Regulations, the Board confirms that no deviation or variation has occurred in the utilisation of proceeds from (i) the Qualified Institutions Placement and (ii) the issue of Convertible Warrants, vis-à-vis the objects stated in the placement document and the shareholders’ approvals. The Audit Committee and the Board reviewed the Monitoring Agency report(s) presented during FY2025 and noted utilisation strictly in line with the stated objects; accordingly, no explanation for variation falls due.

Human Capital: Enabling Excellence, Growth, and Well-being

At Max Estates, our people are at the heart of growth and value creation. In FY2025, we stepped up efforts to build a future-ready, performance-driven, and inclusive workplace. Guided by our purpose to ‘Enhance quality

of life through the spaces we create’, and grounded in the Max Group values of Sevabhav, Credibility, and Excellence, we continued to nurture a workplace that empowers individuals and teams to thrive.

Through a sharper focus on leadership, digital transformation, talent, and employee well-being, we strengthened our people’s practices to grow responsibly, stay agile, while fostering a strong workplace culture.

RISK MANAGEMENT

The Company considers risk management an integral part of its business operations and follows a proactive approach to identify, assess and mitigate risks. Your company has in place the Risk Management Committee to identify the risks impacting the business and formulate strategies and policies for risk mitigation. Further, a central cross-functional team maintains the ‘Risk Register’, which is a framework used to identify and assess key risks, risk probability, risk impact, risk horizon and formulate mitigation strategies in consultation with process owners.

In the ‘Risk Register’, the value chain has been split into seven risk categories: Business, Regulatory, Capital, Macroeconomic, People, Technology and Brand. Each risk is classified into one of these categories. The Risk Register is updated quarterly by the respective process owners, and risk movements are tracked and recorded to strengthen the culture of risk awareness across the organisation.

There are no risks that, in the opinion of the Board, threaten the existence of the Company.

#### Letter to Stakeholders

Dear Stakeholders,

At Max Estates, our mission to "enhance the quality of life through the spaces we create" is more than just rhetorical; it is the driving force behind everything we do. As a leading real estate player in Delhi NCR, we recognize the pivotal role we play in shaping sustainable urban environments and positively impacting the lives of our stakeholders.

From the outset, sustainability has been woven into the fabric of our organization. We understand the urgency of addressing climate change and environmental degradation, which is why we've embarked on a steadfast journey towards sustainability. Our actions are aligned with the global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), as we endeavor to set a new standard for responsible development in the real estate sector.

Our approach to sustainability is comprehensive and dynamic. We've implemented robust measures to boost energy efficiency and optimize resource utilization across all our projects. All our commercial office developments which are already delivered have secured LEED/IGBC Platinum Ratings for Green Building Strategies and WELL Health & Safety Rated. Our upcoming Residential developments including Estate 128 in Noida, and Estate 360 in Gurugram are designed for and pre-certified with IGBC Platinum rating. In addition, for Max Towers we have achieved LEED Operations & Maintenance Platinum certified. Moreover, our upcoming commercial developments including Max 65 in Gurgaon is pre certified LEED Platinum for green building strategies, and Max Square II is pre-certified with IGBC Platinum rating exemplifying our commitment to green building practices.

At the heart of our sustainability strategy lies the seamless integration of nature into our built environment. We prioritize green spaces and innovative landscape designs to foster well-being and combat the adverse effects of urbanization. Estate 128 with its sprawling green cover comprising over 70%, of the development, epitomizes our pledge to create thriving and healthy communities.

Energy, water, waste and biodiversity are critical aspects for Max Estates to address because they significantly influence the environmental footprint of the built environment. Neglecting these areas can exacerbate resource depletion, climate change, pollution, and ecological imbalance, while prioritizing them can contribute to environmental restoration and long-term sustainable development.

At Max Estates, we have aligned our processes towards responsible use and protection of the natural environment through sustainable practices and conservation efforts, aiming to preserve the health and resilience of ecosystems for present and future generations. We have implemented Environment Management System (ISO 14001:2015) in our operations to reduce environmental impact and achieve our environmental goals.

We believe that building designs that prioritize waste management can facilitate reduction, sorting, and recycling of waste, minimizing the environmental footprint are crucial to streamline operations. Spaces dedicated to recycling and organic composting encourage segregation of waste effectively. Combined with diversion of waste from landfill, we champion a sustainable lifestyle for our residents and occupants.

Water conservation is another cornerstone of our sustainability agenda. Recognizing the water challenges faced by urban centers, like Delhi NCR, we've embraced innovative solutions such as recycling water from onsite sewage treatment plants and implementing on-site treatment measures to curb groundwater depletion during construction activities. Innovative building designs can significantly reduce water consumption through the incorporation of efficient fixtures and water reuse systems. At our commercial development, Max Square, we have achieved a zero-waste water discharge facility through our water conservation interventions.

In our unwavering commitment to transparency and accountability, we've published a Sustainability Note & our BRSR report, offering insights into our progress and future aspirations. Moreover, we have adopted global standards, such as GRESB, to benchmark our performance and drive continuous improvement in our environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. We have also begun our journey of computing and monitoring our GHG emissions to ultimately set targets, following the SBTi curriculum, and move towards net zero buildings.

Since 2021, we have been on a structured ESG journey, delineating short-term, medium-term, and long term goals to drive sustainable development. Having successfully achieved our medium-term objectives, we have undertaken a comprehensive review to refine and prioritize our ESG goals for FY26. These goals include:

» Strategize and develop targets for Net Zero emissions » Committing to SBTi for our Net Zero goal » Life Cycle Embodied Carbon Analysis for Max Towers » Explore partnerships to create a circular economy » Source Renewable energy for our delivered commercial assets » Increase gender diversity at Max Estates Head Office level to 25% » Increase participation of women as labour on construction site » Academic tie-ups to increase awareness and interest of women in real estate » Provide dedicated channels for lodging grievances, thereby improving governance and efficient stakeholder management These specific and measurable goals underscore our dedication to advancing sustainability across all facets of our operations, from environmental stewardship to social responsibility and governance. By aligning our actions with these targets, we aim to strengthen our position as a leader in sustainable real estate development and create lasting value for our stakeholders.

Max Estates distinguishes itself in the real estate sector by strongly emphasising ethical conduct. This is achieved by implementing a comprehensive governance framework designed to combat corruption.

A cornerstone of this framework is a robust Whistleblower Policy that encourages the reporting of misconduct and ensures appropriate corrective actions are taken when necessary.

The following publicly available anti-corruption policies underscore Max Estates’ dedication to transparency and ethical operations:

Building a Culture of Integrity These policies ensure that all employees, regardless of their role, understand the importance of ethical conduct. They are embedded into the onboarding process for new hires and are reinforced regularly through emails, training workshops, and ongoing communication.

2. a. Does the entity have procedures in place for sustainable sourcing? (Yes/No) Yes, Max Estates is committed to sustainable sourcing, in line with the company’s long-standing vision and corporate policies for sustainable development within the real estate sector. Our sourcing practices are followed by the principles of green building certification of the highest standards that we aim for, comply with applicable environmental regulations and include ongoing evaluation of sustainably for both structural and non-structural materials. We also actively explore advancements in modular construction technologies and place a strong emphasis on reducing and recycling construction and demolition waste. Additionally, we maintain stringent standards to ensure that all suppliers, manufacturers, and contractors comply with relevant legislation. Max Estates maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards forced, bonded, or child labour across its supply chain. We also promote collaborative partnerships with our suppliers to drive continuous product innovation and minimize environmental impact. Weblink to our Sustainable Procurement Policy.

b. If yes, what percentage of inputs were sourced sustainably? Max Estates mandates that all its developments achieve at least LEED/IGBC Gold certification. In line with this overarching commitment, we adhere to the guidelines set forth by LEED/IGBC for material usage in sustainable buildings. For instance, only low-VOC paints are utilised in our assets, in compliance with LEED/IGBC standards. Additionally, we incorporate (encourage) the use of the materials with GreenPro Ecolabel, which are products that qualify as Green Products.

3. Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling and disposing at the end of life, for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other waste. We only use sustainable and environmentally responsible materials and practices during construction. Specifically, we use AAC Blocks, Fly Ash Bricks, and incorporate fly ash in Ready-Mix Concrete (RMC). Additionally, waste materials such as debris from block work, brickwork, and concrete are reused as filling material at our sites, reducing the need for virgin resources and minimizing construction waste.

A site safety management committee is responsible for monitoring the execution of each safety plan. Regular internal and external safety audits are conducted to ensure compliance with safety guidelines. 12. Describe the measures taken by the entity to ensure a safe and healthy workplace. In alignment with our “WorkWell philosophy”, all of Max Estates’ assets are people-centric, with all possible measures having been incorporated for enhancing workplace health and well-being not only at the design stage but also whilst operating the assets. These measures address various aspects such as indoor air quality, water quality, daylight access, biophilia, hygiene parameters, healthy food choices, lifestyle etc. We ensure safety through structured daily toolbox talks, periodic safety audits, mandatory use of personal protective equipment (PPE), comprehensive emergency response plans, regular safety trainings, and strict adherence to applicable statutory norms.

Max Estates conducts weekly site safety inspections, generating reports based on these inspections. Copies of the completed inspection reports are kept on-site and are available for review at all times. Any deficiencies identified or unsafe practices discovered during these inspections are promptly addressed through remedial actions. Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) is conducted as per the Safety SOP on both routine and non-routine basis.

This collectively helps in promoting physical, psychological, and social well-being among all building occupants. To implement these measures, design, operational and policy level interventions are required which are well incorporated in all the assets.

The entire portfolio adheres to the National Building Code (NBC) 2016, ensuring the safety of both premises and employees.

We have successfully received ISO 9001 certification for Quality Management, ISO 45001 certification for Occupational Health and Safety, and ISO 14001 certification for Environmental Management.
